'''Kerrie Mengersen''' (born 1962)<ref>Birth year from copyright page of ''Handbook of Meta-analysis in Ecology and Evolution'', Princeton University Press, 2013</ref> is an Australian [[Statistics|statistician]]. She is a Professor of Statistics at [[Queensland University of Technology]], and 2024 winner of the [[Ruby Payne-Scott Medal and Lecture]] from the [[Australian Academy of Science]].<ref name=profile/><ref name=praise/><ref name="2024 awardees">{{Cite web |title=2024 awardees {{!}} Australian Academy of Science |url=https://www.science.org.au/supporting-science/awards-and-opportunities-2/honorific-awardees/2024-awardees |access-date=2024-04-05 |website=www.science.org.au |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Mengersen earned BA (Hons I) and PhD degrees in mathematics, majoring in Statistics and Computing, from the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]] (Armidale, New South Wales, Australia) in 1985 and 1989, respectively.<ref name="profile" />  She is the Director of the Bayesian Research and Applications Group (BRAG) within QUT's School of Mathematical Sciences<ref>{{cite web|url = https://research.qut.edu.au/brag/|date=19 February 2026|title=Bayesian Research & Applications Group}}</ref>, a member of the university's Centre for Data Science,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.qut.edu.au/qutcds/people/| date=19 February 2026|title = Centre for Data Science}}</ref> and was Deputy Director of the former Australian Research Council (ARC) Centre of Excellence for Mathematical and Statistical Frontiers (ACEMS) of Big Data, Big Models, New Insights.<ref name="bigdata" />

She has co-authored three books and edited two, and has written 27 book chapters and approximately 250 journal articles.<ref name=brag/><ref name=google/> Her research covers a broad spectrum of statistical practice, from theory<ref>{{Cite Q|Q126310706}}</ref> to its applications.<ref>{{Cite Q|Q126310715}}</ref> She is primarily known for her work in [[Bayesian statistics]] and [[meta-analysis]], and has worked in applications of statistics in [[medicine]] and [[environmental science]].<ref name=dp/> In 2016, she was the first woman to be awarded the Statistical Society of Australia's [[Pitman Medal]], which recognises outstanding achievement in the statistics discipline.<ref name=praise/> She talks about new challenges for statisticians in a YouTube video.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EWeUvqGvgDc|title=Professor Kerrie Mengersen Science Week 2015 Lecture at QUT|last=ACEMS - ARC Centre of Excellence for Mathematical & Statistical Frontiers|date=6 September 2015|via=YouTube|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210124845/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EWeUvqGvgDc|archivedate=10 February 2018}}</ref> She has contributed to Australian [[biosecurity]] efforts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://legacy.crcplantbiosecurity.com.au/users/mengersenk.html|title=Mengersen – CRC for Plant Biosecurity|website=legacy.crcplantbiosecurity.com.au|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304222838/http://legacy.crcplantbiosecurity.com.au/users/mengersenk.html|archivedate=2016-03-04}}</ref>
In October 2015, her research in building virtual [[habitat]]s was highlighted on the [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-10-06/professor-kerrie-mengersen-qut-panoramic-camera-habitat-survey/6831284|title=Professor Kerrie Mengersen with a panoramic camera that is helping to build virtual habitats.|date=6 October 2015|website=ABC News|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210124845/http://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-10-06/professor-kerrie-mengersen-qut-panoramic-camera-habitat-survey/6831284|archivedate=10 February 2018}}</ref>

Mengersen was the National President of the Statistical Society of Australia (SSAI) in 2013, and was the International President of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] (ISBA) in 2016.<ref name="bayesian.org"/> As of 2022, she is a member of the Academy Council of the Queensland Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy Council |url=https://www.qldacademy.org.au/dbpage.php?pg=council |access-date=2022-04-20 |website=Queensland Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* 2014 Elected Fellow of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]]<ref name=fellowsISBA/>
* Elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref name=fellows/>
* Elected Fellow of the [[Society for Modelling and Simulation]]<ref name=sms/>
* 2015 Biennial Medalist of the Modelling and Simulation Society of Australia and New Zealand (MSSANZ)<ref name=MSSANZ/>
* 2015 [[Australian Research Council]] [[Australian Laureate Fellowship|Laureate Fellowship]]<ref name=laureate>{{cite web|url=http://www.arc.gov.au/news-media/media-releases/15-new-australian-laureate-fellows-announced|title=15 new Australian Laureate Fellows announced|last=Anonymous|date=23 June 2015|website=www.arc.gov.au|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160318211940/http://www.arc.gov.au/news-media/media-releases/15-new-australian-laureate-fellows-announced|archivedate=18 March 2016}}</ref>
* 2016 [[Statistical Society of Australia]] Pitman Medal<ref name=praise/>
* 2018 Elected Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] (FAA)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/professor-kerrie-mengersen|title=Professor Kerrie Mengersen|website=www.science.org.au|access-date=2018-06-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616054726/https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/professor-kerrie-mengersen|archive-date=16 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2018 Elected Fellow of the [[Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia]] (FASSA)<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Academy Fellow: Professor Kerrie Mengersen FASSA, FAA|url=https://socialsciences.org.au/academy-fellow/?sId=0032v000033l9TKAAY|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-13|website=Academy of the Social Sciences in Australia|language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2024 [[Ruby Payne-Scott Medal and Lecture]] from the Australian Academy of Science<ref name="2024 awardees"/>
